facts_used: AGENTS.md security boundary and cursor ownership

reasoning_summary: The implementation closes the documented table-07 integration gap with a local control-plane path. Scheduler readiness is dependency/barrier based and deterministic; runtime owns events and the workflow-specific checkpoint stream; workers remain injected/read-only. Approval and kill-switch decisions are fail-closed. Existing contracts remain the source of truth, so a missing or invalid policy/worker result cannot become verified.
alternative_explanations: A passing synthetic callback does not prove a real worker implementation is safe; real network adapters remain intentionally untested.
A completed synthetic graph does not establish production cross-process cancellation or lease renewal semantics.
The current verifier integration validates control-plane readiness; it does not invent a proven finding without Code and Analyst evidence.
hypotheses: Table 07 acceptance requires deterministic local graph execution and durable cursor/event transitions.
Approval and stop controls must be consumed before dispatch and must dominate lower-level allow decisions.
Fan-out/fan-in correctness is best represented by stable IDs and barrier status aggregation rather than raw branch payloads.
unknowns: Whether a future deployment needs a process-backed executor rather than the current in-process executor.
Whether FH will be admitted to formal graph validation in a later table; this implementation preserves run_status.json only in generic runtime mapping.
Operator-specific approval persistence and lease renewal cadence.
